content.text:
The strongest proof slide combines one external benchmark with three measured prototype results.

## Recommended slide

**Why are we the best? Faster to the right answer.**

> **Industry benchmark:** Companies take **two weeks on average** to plan and execute a response after a supply-chain disruption.  
> — [McKinsey Global Supply Chain Leader Survey 2024, n=88](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights/supply-chain-risk-survey-2024)

| **<1 second** | **20.5% lower cost** | **3/3 risks blocked** |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic analysis after quote data arrives | €50.1k versus €63.1k for the obvious on-time split | Blocked origin, expired certification, missing audit |
| 6 suppliers screened, 7 strategies ranked | €12,948 saved while keeping the line running | Every rejection includes its policy reason |

These prototype figures come directly from the [CASE-001 artifacts](/Users/lorenzkrinner/conductor/workspaces/ehl_hack/lahore/ui/lib/fixtures/CASE-001.artifacts.json:2) and [recorded event log](/Users/lorenzkrinner/conductor/workspaces/ehl_hack/lahore/ui/lib/fixtures/CASE-001.events.json:33).

Add this footnote:

> *SupplyOS results are from a deterministic simulated shortage case with rehearsed supplier responses—not yet production customer outcomes.*

I would keep the modelled €5.30M avoided downtime out of the main slide. It is dramatic, but depends on a synthetic €18,400/hour line-stop assumption and could distract from the more defensible proof.

## Other useful external benchmarks

- A typical supplier search takes about **three months and more than 40 hours of sourcing work**. AI-based discovery tools can reduce search time by 90% or more. [McKinsey, 2021](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights/with-artificial-intelligence-find-new-suppliers-in-days-not-months)
- In a survey of 100 large enterprises, **63% reported supplier onboarding taking 15–28 days**, while 31% reported 29–60 days. [HICX Supplier Experience Survey](https://www.hicx.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/REDACTED.pdf)

Treat onboarding as an appendix benchmark because SupplyOS currently prepares the sourcing decision; it does not complete supplier onboarding.

## Metrics to prove real improvement

Instrument these timestamps and compare SupplyOS with the existing manual process:

- **Time to decision-ready plan:** `decision_ready − shortage_detected`
- **Human touch time:** active buyer minutes per shortage, excluding supplier waiting time
- **Time to first qualified quote:** first compliant, complete, deadline-feasible quote
- **Risk-adjusted landed-cost improvement:** compare with the buyer’s best feasible manual plan
- **On-time coverage:** percentage of the shortage covered without stopping production
- **Compliance escape rate:** prohibited suppliers incorrectly advanced; target zero
- **Audit completeness:** cases containing ERP snapshot, quotes, transcripts, calculations, compliance checks, and rationale
- **Qualified quote yield:** usable quotes divided by suppliers contacted

For genuine proof, replay 20–30 historical shortage cases using the information available at the time. Report median and P90, sample size, and manual-versus-SupplyOS results. Until then, call the current result a **timed demonstration**, not a benchmark.

The full sourced research—with additional benchmarks, caveats, and the evaluation methodology—is in [supplyos-proof-benchmarks.md](/Users/lorenzkrinner/conductor/workspaces/ehl_hack/lahore/.context/supplyos-proof-benchmarks.md).

Add this as a benchmark. But in the slide, it said that we don't have actual numbers to prove that ours are not faster. But right now, the first call comes in about 3-5 min, about 15 minutes to get the initial data for all suppliers we need (+X many days needed for all suppliers needed to pick up the phone (if no public data avaiable) and then its up to the humans to decide.

add this useful external benchmarks as well: "A typical supplier search takes about three months and more than 40 hours of sourcing work", ignore the other one

I’ll add a dedicated proof slide that contrasts the external supplier-search benchmark with your measured operating reality: first response in 3–5 minutes, initial supplier data in about 15 minutes, supplier availability as the remaining variable, and a human retaining the final decision. I’m using the impeccable UI skill so the new slide reads as evidence, not as a dense metrics dump.
